title: Thunder Substack (by Andreea Popa): Values only count when living them costs you something
summary: Andreea writes that values are proven only when they are inconvenient; otherwise they are just preferences. She extends this to forgiving others who are still growing, and to choosing what you pay attention to, using David Foster Wallace's "This Is Water". It is her reflection; she only references Cris's earlier newsletter on seeing the invisible.

principles.text: Values are tested by cost: if living them is always easy, they are only preferences.
principles.quote: That's the thing about values - they only mean something when they're tested. If it's always easy, always convenient, maybe it's not really a value yet. Maybe it's just a preference.

principles.text: Real values often feel like choosing against your ego, and many are chosen in solitude.
principles.quote: real values show up when picking them feels like choosing against your ego.

principles.text: Be honest about chasing the feeling of being good versus carrying the weight of living it.
principles.quote: I saw how often I was chasing the feeling of being good, not the weight of actually living it.

principles.text: Extend grace: accept people as they are today, not the version you wish they were.
principles.quote: Can I accept the version of them that exists today, not the one I wish they already were?

principles.text: Forgiveness means not reducing someone to their worst moment.
principles.quote: Forgiveness is not pretending the hurt didn't happen. It's choosing not to reduce someone to their worst moment.

principles.text: Choose your attention deliberately, or the world will choose it for you.
principles.quote: Because if you don't choose your attention, the world will choose for you.
